request.prompt:
Job X1: usp_broker_production. Parameters per run, in order: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job      : rpt.usp_broker_production
  3 |   Purpose  : Broker production report for distribution MI. One row per broker
  4 |              and line of business as at @AsOfDate: policies in force, gross
  5 |              written premium in EUR booked in the calendar year, claims notified
  6 |              and claims paid in the year, and a review flag for brokers whose
  7 |              paid-to-written ratio for the year is above 0.75.
  8 |   Author   : PdeB
  9 |   Change log
 10 |     2014-02-10  PdeB  Initial version (CR-0412)
 11 |     2015-09-03  PdeB  GBP/USD premium converted to EUR at the ECB rate (CR-0688)
 12 |     2017-11-20  SOK   Direct business reported under broker code DIRECT (CR-1047)
 13 |     2019-05-14  AMcG  Inactive brokers kept when they still have business (INC-2231)
 14 |     2021-03-08  SOK   Paid-to-written review flag for distribution (CR-1590)
 15 |     2022-06-27  AMcG  Broker codes trimmed and upper-cased (INC-3118)
 16 | ==============================================================================*/
 17 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 18 | GO
 19 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'rpt.broker_production', N'U') IS NULL
 20 | CREATE TABLE rpt.broker_production (
 21 |     as_of_date         DATE           NOT NULL,
 22 |     broker_code        VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
 23 |     broker_name        NVARCHAR(80)   NULL,
 24 |     broker_status      VARCHAR(10)    NULL,
 25 |     lob_code           VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 26 |     policies_in_force  INT            NOT NULL,
 27 |     gwp_eur            DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 28 |     claims_notified    INT            NOT NULL,
 29 |     claims_paid_eur    DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 30 |     paid_to_written    DECIMAL(12,4)  NULL,
 31 |     review_flag        CHAR(1)        NOT NULL
 32 | );
 33 | GO
 34 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE rpt.usp_broker_production
 35 |     @AsOfDate DATE
 36 | AS
 37 | BEGIN
 38 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 39 | 
 40 |     DECLARE @job       VARCHAR(128) = 'rpt.usp_broker_production';
 41 |     DECLARE @YearStart DATE         = DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(@AsOfDate), 1, 1);
 42 |     DECLARE @rows      INT;
 43 | 
 44 |     BEGIN TRY
 45 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 46 | 
 47 |         -- policy attributes from the latest snapshot on or before the as-of date
 48 |         SELECT x.policy_id, x.broker_code, x.lob_code, x.inception_date, x.expiry_date, x.cancellation_date
 49 |         INTO #pol
 50 |         FROM (
 51 |             SELECT s.policy_id,
 52 |                    ISNULL(UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(s.broker_code))), 'DIRECT') AS broker_code,
 53 |                    UPPER(RTRIM(p.lob_code)) AS lob_code,
 54 |                    s.inception_date, s.expiry_date, s.cancellation_date,
 55 |                    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.policy_id
 56 |                                       ORDER BY s.snapshot_date DESC, s._row_seq DESC) AS rn
 57 |             FROM stg.policy_snapshots s WITH (NOLOCK)
 58 |             INNER JOIN stg.products p WITH (NOLOCK) ON p.product_code = s.product_code
 59 |             WHERE s.snapshot_date <= @AsOfDate
 60 |         ) x
 61 |         WHERE x.rn = 1;
 62 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 63 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'policies', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 64 | 
 65 |         -- policies in force on the as-of date
 66 |         SELECT p.broker_code, p.lob_code, COUNT(*) AS policies_in_force
 67 |         INTO #inforce
 68 |         FROM #pol p
 69 |         WHERE p.inception_date <= @AsOfDate
 70 |           AND p.expiry_date >= @AsOfDate
 71 |           AND (p.cancellation_date IS NULL OR p.cancellation_date > @AsOfDate)
 72 |         GROUP BY p.broker_code, p.lob_code;
 73 | 
 74 |         -- premium booked in the year, at the latest rate published on or before the booking date
 75 |         SELECT p.broker_code, p.lob_code,
 76 |                SUM(t.amount * CASE WHEN t.currency = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx.rate_to_eur END) AS gwp_eur
 77 |         INTO #gwp
 78 |         FROM stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
 79 |         INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = t.policy_id
 80 |         OUTER APPLY (
 81 |             SELECT TOP 1 f.rate_to_eur
 82 |             FROM stg.fx_rates f WITH (NOLOCK)
 83 |             WHERE f.currency = t.currency
 84 |               AND f.rate_date <= t.txn_date
 85 |             ORDER BY f.rate_date DESC, f._row_seq DESC
 86 |         ) fx
 87 |         WHERE t.txn_date >= @YearStart
 88 |           AND t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate
 89 |         GROUP BY p.broker_code, p.lob_code;
 90 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 91 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'premium', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 92 | 
 93 |         -- claims notified in the year
 94 |         SELECT c.claim_id, p.broker_code, p.lob_code
 95 |         INTO #clm
 96 |         FROM stg.claims c WITH (NOLOCK)
 97 |         INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
 98 |         WHERE c.reported_date >= @YearStart
 99 |           AND c.reported_date <= @AsOfDate;
100 | 
101 |         SELECT c.broker_code, c.lob_code, COUNT(*) AS claims_notified
102 |         INTO #notified
103 |         FROM #clm c
104 |         GROUP BY c.broker_code, c.lob_code;
105 | 
106 |         -- claims paid in the year, recoveries netted off, unkeyed amounts ignored
107 |         SELECT c.broker_code, c.lob_code, SUM(ISNULL(cp.amount, 0)) AS claims_paid_eur
108 |         INTO #paid
109 |         FROM stg.claim_payments cp WITH (NOLOCK)
110 |         INNER JOIN #clm c ON c.claim_id = cp.claim_id
111 |         WHERE cp.payment_date >= @YearStart
112 |           AND cp.payment_date <= @AsOfDate
113 |         GROUP BY c.broker_code, c.lob_code;
114 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
115 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'claims', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
116 | 
117 |         SELECT broker_code, lob_code INTO #keys FROM #inforce
118 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #gwp
119 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #notified
120 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #paid;
121 | 
122 |         -- paid-to-written ratio over all lines of the broker
123 |         SELECT k.broker_code,
124 |                CAST(SUM(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0)), 0) AS DECIMAL(12,4)) AS paid_to_written
125 |         INTO #ratio
126 |         FROM #keys k
127 |         LEFT JOIN #gwp g   ON g.broker_code = k.broker_code AND g.lob_code = k.lob_code
128 |         LEFT JOIN #paid pd ON pd.broker_code = k.broker_code AND pd.lob_code = k.lob_code
129 |         GROUP BY k.broker_code;
130 | 
131 |         TRUNCATE TABLE rpt.broker_production;
132 | 
133 |         INSERT INTO rpt.broker_production
134 |             (as_of_date, broker_code, broker_name, broker_status, lob_code, policies_in_force,
135 |              gwp_eur, claims_notified, claims_paid_eur, paid_to_written, review_flag)
136 |         SELECT @AsOfDate,
137 |                k.broker_code,
138 |                b.broker_name,
139 |                UPPER(RTRIM(b.status)),
140 |                k.lob_code,
141 |                ISNULL(i.policies_in_force, 0),
142 |                CAST(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),
143 |                ISNULL(n.claims_notified, 0),
144 |                CAST(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),
145 |                r.paid_to_written,
146 |                CASE WHEN r.paid_to_written > 0.75 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END
147 |         FROM #keys k
148 |         LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK) ON b.broker_code = k.broker_code
149 |         LEFT JOIN #inforce i  ON i.broker_code = k.broker_code AND i.lob_code = k.lob_code
150 |         LEFT JOIN #gwp g      ON g.broker_code = k.broker_code AND g.lob_code = k.lob_code
151 |         LEFT JOIN #notified n ON n.broker_code = k.broker_code AND n.lob_code = k.lob_code
152 |         LEFT JOIN #paid pd    ON pd.broker_code = k.broker_code AND pd.lob_code = k.lob_code
153 |         LEFT JOIN #ratio r    ON r.broker_code = k.broker_code;
154 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
155 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'load rpt.broker_production', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
156 | 
157 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
158 |     END TRY
159 |     BEGIN CATCH
160 |         DECLARE @msg NVARCHAR(4000) = ERROR_MESSAGE(), @err INT = ERROR_NUMBER();
161 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
162 |              @message = @msg, @error_number = @err;
163 |         THROW;
164 |     END CATCH
165 | END;
166 | GO

Input tables:
- stg.policy_snapshots: snapshot_date DATE NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, policy_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, broker_code VARCHAR(10), inception_date DATE NOT NULL, expiry_date DATE NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, cancellation_date DATE, annual_premium DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, sum_insured DECIMAL(14,2), payment_frequency VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, vehicle_reg VARCHAR(12), ncd_years INT
- stg.products: product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, product_name NVARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, lob_code VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL, term_months INT, levy_rate DECIMAL(5,4) NOT NULL, launched_on DATE NOT NULL, withdrawn_on DATE
- stg.premium_transactions: txn_id INT NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, txn_type VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL, txn_date DATE NOT NULL, effective_from DATE NOT NULL, effective_to DATE NOT NULL, amount DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL
- stg.fx_rates: rate_date DATE NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, rate_to_eur DECIMAL(18,8) NOT NULL, source VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL
- stg.claims: claim_id INT NOT NULL, claim_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, lob_code VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL, loss_date DATE NOT NULL, reported_date DATE NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, closed_date DATE, cause_code VARCHAR(10), handler_code VARCHAR(8), description NVARCHAR(200)
- stg.claim_payments: payment_id INT NOT NULL, claim_id INT NOT NULL, payment_date DATE NOT NULL, amount DECIMAL(12,2), payment_type VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, payee_type VARCHAR(12)
- stg.brokers: broker_code CHAR(6) NOT NULL, broker_name NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, region VARCHAR(20), commission_rate DECIMAL(5,4) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, appointed_date DATE NOT NULL

Semantic traps to test (one case per distinct trap id):
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 58-58: The products join compares the raw VARCHAR product_code values without any normalisation. Under the CI collation, case variants match; in Spark they would not, so policies would drop out of the inner join.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 58-58: The product_code join ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark needs an rtrim on both sides or padded codes miss the inner join.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 76-76: t.currency is CHAR(3) text, so currency = 'EUR' also matches 'eur'/'Eur' under the CI collation. A binary comparison in Spark would route those rows to the fx rate instead.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 76-76: currency is CHAR(3) and the comparison ignores trailing spaces (e.g. 'EUR ' or a padded short code). Spark compares exactly.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 76-76: amount DECIMAL(12,2) * rate DECIMAL(18,8), summed. The result's precision and scale must match legacy before the final rounding to 2dp.
- TSQL-08 (TOP and TOP WITH TIES) at lines 81-85: TOP 1 ordered by rate_date DESC, _row_seq DESC. The order is deterministic as long as _row_seq is unique per date, and the Spark window must use the same tie-break.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 83-83: The fx lookup matches f.currency = t.currency, two text columns from different sources, case-insensitively. In Spark, case variants would find no rate and the premium would come out NULL.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 83-83: The CHAR(3) currency match ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark matches exactly unless both sides are trimmed.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 124-124: DECIMAL(38,2)/DECIMAL(38,2) division is cut down to scale 6 in SQL Server and then rounded to DECIMAL(12,4), so the value is rounded twice. Spark's decimal division and cast must give the same ratio, which feeds the 0.75 flag.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 142-142: The high-scale gwp sum is cast to DECIMAL(14,2), rounding half away from zero. Spark must cast the decimal and must not round a double.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 144-144: Claims paid is cast to DECIMAL(14,2). Spark must keep decimal types (not double) so the result matches.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 148-148: stg.brokers.broker_code is not normalised, but k.broker_code is upper-cased. The CI join still matches lower- or mixed-case broker codes; a binary Spark join would lose broker_name and status.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 148-148: stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6), so it is padded with spaces and may also carry stored trailing spaces. SQL Server's join ignores them, while Spark needs rtrim on b.broker_code to match the trimmed key.
request.system_prompt:
You are the test author agent of LANSH, a factory that migrates legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) jobs to PySpark and must reproduce their output exactly. For each semantic trap you are given, write one small input set (5 to 20 rows per table) on which a naive translation of this job would give a different result from the legacy engine, while the job still produces output rows.

- Use only the job's input tables and their columns; respect each column's legacy type and length (a VARCHAR(5) value has at most 5 characters) and fill every NOT NULL column.
- Write every value as text: dates YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, numbers as plain decimals; use null for NULL. Leave _row_seq out: the rows' order is their _row_seq.
- Include the related rows the job needs to produce output (for example, a claim's payments) and rows on both sides of the trap (the variant that a naive translation mishandles, and the canonical value).
- The expected output is computed by running the legacy job itself on your rows, so never state expected values.

cases.description: Line 58: the snapshots carry product_code in different cases ('mot01', 'Mot01', 'hom01', 'pRODUCT' style), but stg.products only has upper-case codes. Under the CI collation, SQL Server joins all of them, so they count in policies_in_force. A binary Spark join drops them. Policies 1, 4 and 6 are the upper-case controls.

Line 58: some snapshot product_codes carry trailing spaces ('MOT01 ', 'MOT01  ', 'HOM01 '), and one products row is stored as 'PET01 ' while its snapshot says 'PET01'. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces, so every policy joins. A Spark equality without rtrim loses policies 2, 3, 5 and 6. Policies 1 and 4 are the unpadded controls.

Line 76: premium transactions in currency 'eur', 'Eur' and 'eUR'. Under CI, they match currency = 'EUR' and are taken at a factor of 1. fx_rates also holds an EUR rate of 1.1. A binary CASE sends these rows to the fx lookup, where they either find no rate (the premium becomes NULL and drops out) or get the 1.1 rate. Either way gwp_eur changes. The 'EUR' and 'GBP' rows are controls.

Line 76: currency is CHAR(3), so a full 'EUR' cannot also carry a trailing space within the column length. The case uses padded short codes instead: 'US ' and 'GB ' are compared against 'EUR' in the CASE and then go to the fx lookup, where fx_rates has 'US' and 'GB' without padding. The 'EUR' rows are controls, and fx_rates holds an EUR rate of 1.1 so that any EUR row wrongly sent to the fx rate shows up. A Spark comparison that does not trim padded CHAR values does not match these rows the way SQL Server does.

Line 76: amount DECIMAL(12,2) times rate DECIMAL(18,8), summed per broker and LOB. For BRK001/MOTOR, 0.50*1.001 plus 0.50*1.009 sums to exactly 1.005. For BRK001/HOME, three 333.33*0.33333333 pieces sum to 333.3299966667. The other rows use high-scale rates and a negative adjustment. If the math is done in double, sums like 1.005 drift below the half and round to 1.00 instead of the decimal 1.01.

Lines 81-85: fx_rates has two GBP rows dated 2025-03-01 (1.15, then 1.17) and two USD rows dated 2025-03-01 (0.90, then 0.92). The TOP 1 picks the row with the higher _row_seq on the tied date. There is also a GBP rate dated after one transaction, which must not be used, and an earlier GBP rate for a February transaction. A Spark window that does not break ties by _row_seq DESC, or uses a non-deterministic first(), can pick the wrong rate.

Line 83: the transaction currencies 'gbp' and 'Gbp' must match fx 'GBP', and transaction 'USD' must match fx rows stored as 'Usd' and 'usd'. Under CI, SQL Server finds the latest rate for each. A binary Spark match finds no rate, so the premium is NULL and those groups get gwp 0. The 'GBP' and 'EUR' rows are controls.

Line 83: CHAR(3) padded short codes. Transaction 'GB ' must match fx 'GB', transaction 'GB' must match the later fx 'GB ' row, and transaction 'US' must match fx 'US '. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces and finds the rate. An exact Spark match finds none, so the premium is NULL. The 'GBP' and 'EUR' rows are controls.

Line 124: the broker-level paid/written ratio sits right at the 0.75 threshold. BRK001: 15000.99/20000 = 0.7500495, which is rounded to 6dp by the division and then to 4dp by the cast. BRK002: 7500.01/10000 = 0.750001, which rounds to 0.7500, so the flag is N even though the raw value is above 0.75. BRK003 spans two LOBs, 7500.50/10000 = 0.75005, which rounds half up to 0.7501, so Y. BRK004 is exactly 0.75. A null payment and a payment after the as-of date are excluded. A double or unrounded ratio flips the flags.

Line 142: each group's high-scale gwp lands exactly on a half cent. 1.00*1.125 = 1.125 should give 1.13, -1.00*1.125 = -1.125 should give -1.13 (half away from zero), 5.00*1.125 = 5.625 should give 5.63, and 3.00*1.165 = 3.495 and 1.00*1.165 = 1.165 should give 3.50 and 1.17. Banker's rounding or rounding through a double gives 1.12, -1.12, 5.62, 3.49 and 1.16. The EUR group is the control.

Line 144: claims paid summed as decimal. Claim 1 has ten payments of 0.10, which sum to 0.9999999999999999 in double. Claim 2 has 100.00, a -25.50 recovery and a NULL amount. Claim 3 has three payments of 1.15, which sum to 3.4499999999999997 in double. Decimal gives exactly 1.00 and 3.45. Double plus truncation or a cast can give 0.99 and 3.44. Claim 4 has no payments, and claim 5 was reported in 2024 and is excluded.

Line 148: the report key broker_code is trimmed and upper-cased, but stg.brokers stores 'brk001', 'Brk002', 'bRK003' and 'direct'. Under CI, SQL Server joins them and fills broker_name and status. A binary Spark join leaves both NULL. BRK004 is the exact-match control. Policy 2's snapshot code is lower case, and policy 4 has a NULL broker_code, which becomes DIRECT.

Line 148: brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) and holds space-padded values ('BRK01 ', 'BRK2  ', 'AB    ', 'DIRECT') that must match the trimmed keys 'BRK01', 'BRK2' and 'AB'. Policy 2's snapshot code ' BRK2 ' is trimmed in the key. SQL Server ignores the trailing spaces and fills broker_name and status. A Spark join without rtrim on b.broker_code leaves them NULL. BRK003 and DIRECT are full-width controls.
